sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The gentry is a euphemistic name for the fairies. In Irish the term is Daoine Uaisle. Humans used such soft names because they feared fairy power. The people behind these names are the Tuatha Dé Danann. Other euphemisms include the Daoine Maithe, the Good People. Another is the Áes Sídhe, the People of the Fairy Mounds. Humans also said the Wee Folk, the Hill Crowd, and the Red Caps. The gentry is a cross-reference to the FAIRY entry.
